summary_findings: Malayalam runs the full 27-nakshatra series in Dravidianised form — Aśvati, Bharaṇi, Kārttika, Rōhiṇi, Makayiram, Tiruvātira … Iravati — and it still governs birth-star reckoning: Gundert 1872 already lexicalises ജന്മനക്ഷത്രം 'the asterism under which one is born' (p. 403) and അനുജന്മനക്ഷത്രം 'the 10th and 19th asterisms after it' (p. 28), and the ordinary word for a birth-star is not the Sanskrit നക്ഷത്രം but the inherited Dravidian നാള്‍ nāḷ 'day', whose illustrative phrase in Gundert is 'to settle [a marriage] after examining the nāḷ and the compatibility' (p. 547). Those names are recorded here compactly, in one collective entry plus nine individually; the real yield is elsewhere. Malayalam's vernacular sky is built on മീന്‍ mīn 'star/fish' (DEDR 4876) — കൊളളിമീന്‍ 'firebrand-star' meteor, വാല്‍മീന്‍ 'tail-star' comet, വെണ്മീന്‍ 'white star' and പെരുമീന്‍ 'great star' for Venus, beside വെള്ളി veḷḷi 'silver = Venus = Friday' and the North Malabar dialect word കൊററി koṟṟi 'morning star', which has no Sanskrit counterpart at all. Two Malayalam finds have no parallel in the other three languages: ഞേങ്ങോല്‍ ñēṅṅōl 'plough-shaft', cross-referenced by Gundert to മുഴക്കോല്‍ 'measuring-rod', a constellation defined purely by its farming use — it rises in Dhanu an hour after sunset and tells the cultivator when to drain the field before sowing (p. 413; probably but not certainly Orion's Belt) — and the ñāṟṟu system, ഞാററുതല / ഞാററുവേലി / ഞായററുനില, the twenty-seven asterism-periods of 13 4/9 days each by which the Kerala farming year is still divided, with Tiruvātira at the burst of the south-west monsoon as 'best time for planting' (pp. 411–412, 436). NEGATIVE: no navigational star name was found for Kerala in any public-domain source — Gundert has no star under 'mariner', 'sailor' or 'compass', Logan's Malabar Manual has none, and the words Pleiades, Orion, Canopus, Sirius, Arcturus, pole star and Milky Way do not occur once in all seven volumes of Thurston. Tulu and Kodava are nearly empty of star names, and that is the result rather than a failure: each has exactly ONE native star-word, the reflex of Dravidian *veḷ 'white' — Tulu ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ boḷḷi 'a star; silver' (Männer 1886 p. 502), forming ತಂಜದ ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ 'the evening star' (p. 262), and Kodava boḷḷi in boḷḷi mi·nï 'morning star' (DEDR 5496) and ಬೊಳ್ಳಿಳಾಚೆ boḷḷiáche 'Friday' (Cole 1867 p. 136) — Tulu naming Venus at dusk and Kodagu at dawn. Kodava has no word for 'star' anywhere in Cole's grammar, no name for the Pleiades, Orion, the pole star, the Milky Way, a comet or a meteor, and DEDR gives it mi·nï only inside that one compound; Tulu adds only three descriptive coinages, all from Männer's English-to-Tulu direction — ಹೊರಸಿನ್ಟ ನಕ್ಷತ್ರೊಳಿ ಕೂಟ 'the star-cluster of the COT' for Ursa Major (the one indigenous constellation image in either language), ನಕ್ಷತ್ರೊಳಿ ಸಾಲ್ 'row of stars' for the Milky Way, and ಆಕಾಶೊಡ್ಡು ಬೂರ್ದಿ ಕಲ್ಲ್ 'stone fallen from the sky' for a meteorite. Neither language times agriculture by a star: Sturrock says all Tulu cultivation runs on the twelve solar months, which have native Tulu names (Paggu, Besha, Kártél, Áte…) that are not star-names (1894 p. 216), Coorg ploughing begins on the first of yaḍamyáru whatever the rain (Cole p. 135), and the Huttari harvest is fixed by the full moon. Sinhala, the comparative control, gives the sharpest answer: it replaced NONE of the twenty-seven — Carter's formula for each is literally 'E. of', Eḷu form of, and Clough's is 'Elu form of', so asvida is Sanskrit aśvinī, denaṭa is dhaniṣṭhā, deṭa is jyeṣṭhā, all merely sound-shifted — while coining freely OUTSIDE that list: හත්·දින්න hat·dinna 'seven-produced' for the Pleiades, අහස් ගඟ ahas gaṅga 'sky-river' for the Milky Way (a calque, per Jayatilaka, of ākāśagaṅgā — the compound Malayalam and Tulu simply borrowed), ඉරබටු තරුව 'star after sunset' and පහන් තරුව 'dawn-star' for Venus, දුම්·කෙහෙලිය 'smoke-banner' for a comet, කළමුනිදුතරුව for Canopus, and three native words for 'constellation' (තරු·වැළ, තරු·පොකුර, උළු කැන) where Malayalam has none. What was portable, then, was the nakshatra list and the learned Sanskrit stock — Dhruva, Agastya/Agasti, Saptarṣi, Ākāśagaṅgā, Ulkā, Dhūmaketu travel intact into all four — and what was not portable was the ordinary night sky, which every language named for itself out of fish, silver, firebrands, plough-beams, cots and river-water.

entries.literal_meaning: 'fish'; also 'that which glitters' (Gundert derives it from മിന്‍ 'to glitter')
entries.usage_note: The inherited Dravidian word for a star. It is the productive element in the vernacular sky vocabulary: കൊളളിമീന്‍ meteor, വാല്‍മീന്‍ comet, വെണ്മീന്‍/വെഴ്മീന്‍/പെരുമീന്‍ Venus.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (Mangalore, 1872), s.v. മീന്‍ mīn, p. 822
entries.quote: മീന്‍ mīn‍ mīǹ 5. (VN. of മിന്‍ ) glittering, sparkling. 1. A fish ... 2. a star. മീ. വീഴുക a meteor.
entries.notes: Homonymy of 'fish' and 'star' is pan-Dravidian and is the semantic engine behind almost every native Malayalam sky-name below. Gundert's own etymology ties both senses to മിന്‍ 'glitter', so the star sense need not be metaphorical from the fish.

entries.usage_note: Used with the verb വീഴുക 'to fall': കൊളളിമീന്‍ വീഴുക 'a meteor falls'. Gundert also records അശനിക്കൊളളിമീന്‍ 'thunderbolt-firebrand-star' from Kṛṣṇagāthā, in a list of portents alongside earthquake.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. കൊളളി koḷḷi, p. 310 (also s.v. മീന്‍, p. 822)
entries.quote: കൊളളിമിന്നല്‍ lightning. കൊളളിമീന്‍ വീഴുക meteor.
entries.notes: Wholly native: both elements are Dravidian, and the same compound type recurs in കൊളളിമിന്നല്‍ 'lightning' and കൊളളിയന്‍ 'a demon with a torch, ignis fatuus'. Malayalam therefore has a native meteor word beside the Sanskrit ഉല്ക.

entries.usage_note: Gundert marks it V1 (Visscher/older vocabularies), i.e. attested in the earlier Malabar word-lists rather than only in literature.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. വാല്‍ vāl, p. 938
entries.quote: വാല്‍നക്ഷത്രം, വാല്‍മീന്‍ a comet V1.
entries.notes: Printed together with the hybrid വാല്‍നക്ഷത്രം (native വാല്‍ + Sanskrit നക്ഷത്രം), which is the form that has survived into modern standard Malayalam; വാല്‍മീന്‍ is the fully native member of the pair.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. വാല്‍ vāl, p. 938
entries.quote: വാല്‍നക്ഷത്രം, വാല്‍മീന്‍ a comet V1.
entries.notes: Hybrid coinage: the compound is formed in Malayalam (Sanskrit uses ധൂമകേതു, केतु, not *पुच्छनक्षत्र), so it counts as vernacular formation even though the head noun is a loan. This is the ordinary word for comet in Malayalam today.

entries.usage_note: An omen-word: Gundert glosses it 'a threatening meteor' and quotes a line meaning 'suddenly from the sky, the ku[ṟakkoḷḷi]'.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. കുറ kuṟa, p. 270
entries.quote: കുറക്കൊള്ളി a threatening meteor, comet (?) ആകാശത്തില്‍ നിന്നുടന്‍ കു. Sk.
entries.notes: Gundert's own question mark: he is unsure whether the referent is a meteor or a comet. Registered here as disputed for that reason. The first element കുറ 'defect, blemish, disgrace' makes it an ill-omen term rather than a neutral astronomical label.

entries.usage_note: Simultaneously 'silver', 'Venus' and 'Friday' — the planet names the weekday, as in വെള്ളിയാഴ്ച Friday, which Gundert notes is the day 'when women & cows must not journey'.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. വെള്ളി veḷḷi, p. 987
entries.quote: വെള്ളി veḷḷi veḷḷi T. M. C. (Tu. boḷḷi, Te. veṇḍi). 1. Silver ... 2. Venus; Friday = ശൂക്രന്‍.
entries.notes: Gundert gives the Dravidian cognate set in the same line — Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada veḷḷi, Tulu boḷḷi, Telugu veṇḍi — establishing the word as inherited, not borrowed. The 'silver' → 'Venus' → 'Friday' chain is independent of Sanskrit śukra, which Malayalam also has (ശുക്രന്‍, p. 1017) as a learned doublet. Gundert's line is evidence for the Tulu form boḷḷi in the sense 'silver'; he does not there assign Tulu the planet sense.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. വെണ്‍ veṇ, p. 981
entries.quote: വെണ്മീന്‍ V2. Venus = വെള്ളി .
entries.notes: A second native Venus name, transparently 'the white star', marked V2 (an older Malabar vocabulary). Gundert prints a further variant വെഴ്മീന്‍ veḻmīn at the end of the വെള്ളി article, p. 987: 'വെഴ്മീന്‍ = വെള്ളി 2., V1.'

entries.usage_note: Specifically the morning apparition of Venus.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. പെരുക്കുക perukkuka, p. 701 (sub-entry പെരുമീന്‍)
entries.quote: പെരുമീന്‍ 1. the morning star, Venus Vl. 2. the large sheat-fish B.
entries.notes: The two senses in the single entry — 'morning star' and 'the large sheat-fish' — are the മീന്‍ homonymy in miniature. Malayalam thus distinguishes the morning star lexically (പെരുമീന്‍, കൊററി) from Venus generally (വെള്ളി, വെണ്മീന്‍); Gundert records no separate evening-star word.

entries.usage_note: North Malabar dialect (Gundert's 'No.' = Northern). Used with the verb of rising: കൊററി ഉദിച്ചു 'the morning star has risen' — the phrase of a rural day beginning.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. കൊററം koṟṟam, p. 309 (sub-entry കൊററി, sense 3)
entries.quote: കൊററി (T. the goddess Durga) l. a young one. — a ewe; a stork. So. MC. ... 3. morning- star, കൊററി ഉദിച്ചു No.
entries.notes: Marked 'likely' because Gundert says only 'morning star', without naming the body; the morning star is normally Venus but Jupiter and Mercury are so called too. The headword's other senses (Tamil Koṟṟavai, the war-goddess; a young animal; a stork) leave the motivation for the star sense unrecovered. This is the most purely local item in the Malayalam set — a North Malabar word with no Sanskrit counterpart at all.

entries.sky_object: a constellation used to time sowing

modern_star.common_name: unidentified — probably the three stars of Orion's Belt

entries.usage_note: An agricultural time-marker. Gundert: it rises in the month of Dhanu (mid-December to mid-January) about an hour after sunset, and its rising tells the cultivator when to do ചക്രം ചവിട്ടുക — 'to clear a ricefield of water preparatory to sowing' (Gundert s.v. ചക്രം, p. 340).
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഞേങ്ങോല്‍ ñēṅṅōl, p. 413 (sense 3)
entries.quote: ഞേങ്ങോല്‍ ñēṅṅō̄l‍ ńēṇṇōl (T. ഞാഞ്ചില്‍ , M. നേ ഞ്ഞില്‍ , Te. നാഗില്‍ , C. നേഗില്‍ , Tu. നായര്‍ ) 1.Plough-shaft ... 3. a constellation മുഴക്കോല്‍ rising in Dhanu an hour aftor sunset & indicating the time for treading the wheel previous to sowing (see ചക്രം ചവിട്ടുക ).
entries.notes: The single most valuable item here: a Malayalam constellation named from a farm implement, defined by its use rather than by any Sanskrit asterism, and cross-referenced by Gundert to a second implement-name, മുഴക്കോല്‍ 'measuring-rod' (p. 846). A short straight row of stars is what both names describe. Orion's Belt fits the stated datum well — in mid-December it clears the eastern horizon roughly an hour after sunset — but Gundert names no stars and no other source consulted repeats the identification, so it is left disputed. Note also that Gundert's Tulu cognate for the implement is നായര്‍ nāyar, not a star word.

entries.sky_object: a constellation used to time sowing
entries.literal_meaning: 'cubit-rod, measuring rod' (മുഴം a cubit + കോല്‍ rod) — the carpenter's 24-finger measure
entries.usage_note: Second name of the same asterism as ഞേങ്ങോല്‍; the agricultural use is given at that entry.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. മുഴം muḻam, p. 846 (sub-entry മുഴക്കോല്‍, sense 2)
entries.quote: മുഴക്കോല്‍ CS. 1. ആശാരിക്കോല്‍ carpenter's rod of 24 വിരല്‍ . 2. the constellation ഞെ ങ്ങോല്‍ .
entries.notes: Both Malayalam names for this asterism are craftsmen's straight-edges — a plough-beam and a carpenter's rule. That two independent entries in Gundert cross-reference each other rules out a printing slip.

entries.sky_object: the asterism-period (rain-period) system of the agricultural year
entries.literal_meaning: 'the head/beginning of the ñāṟṟu' — ñāṟṟu being both 'rice seedling' and the sun's station
entries.usage_note: The Kerala farming calendar: the solar year is divided into stretches during which the sun stands in one asterism, each stretch named after that asterism and each carrying its own agricultural prescription. Gundert's worked example is തിരുവാതിരഞാററുതല, the Ārdrā period at the start of Mithunam (mid-June), 'best time for planting' — the onset of the south-west monsoon.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഞാറു ñāṟu, p. 412; and s.v. തല tala, p. 436
entries.quote: ഞാററുതല (2) the time of a constellation f. i. തിരു വാതിരഞാ . in the beginning of Mithuna, best time for planting. അത്തംഞാ . feast in Kanni.
entries.notes: Gundert defines the unit precisely under തല, p. 436: 'a point of time, as the influence of a star, the rule of an asterism (= 13 4/9 days) തിരുവാതിര ഞാററു തല' — 13 4/9 days being 365.25 ÷ 27. He also gives ഞാററുനില and ഞാററുവട്ടം as further names of the same thing, and under ഞായറു (p. 411) the underlying definition തിരുവാതിരഞായററു നില, 'the sun's position in a constellation'. This is the ñāṟṟuveḷa scheme, attested in the standard dictionary of 1872 and still in farming use.

entries.sky_object: the asterism-period (rain-period) system of the agricultural year
entries.usage_note: The days within an asterism-period that are fixed on for transplanting rice.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഞാറു ñāṟu, p. 412 (sub-entries ഞാററുവാല, ഞാററുവേലി)
entries.quote: ഞാററുവാല , — വേലി V1. days fixed upon for transplanting.
entries.notes: This is Gundert's printing of the word that modern Malayalam writes ഞാറ്റുവേല ñāṟṟuvēla, the name of the twenty-seven asterism rain-periods. Marked 'likely' because Gundert prints വേലി (with retroflex l and final i) rather than വേല, and glosses it only as 'days fixed upon for transplanting'; whether the two are the same word or a near-homophone is not settled by this entry alone.

modern_star.bayer: λ, φ¹, φ² Orionis and neighbours

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഇന്വകകള്‍ invakakaḷ, p. 108
entries.quote: ഇന്വകകള്‍ invakakaḷ‍ invaγaγaḷ Tdbh. ഇല്വക S. 5 Stars in the head of Orion.
entries.notes: A striking survival: Gundert marks it a tadbhava of Sanskrit ilvakā (Vedic Ilvalāḥ / Invakāḥ, the old name of Mṛgaśiras), a word that is archaic even in Sanskrit. Malayalam keeps it with a native plural in -kaḷ. Gundert's count of five differs from the three or five usually given for the Vedic asterism; 'likely' rather than 'certain' for that reason.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. അഗസ്തി agasti, p. 6
entries.quote: അഗസ്തി agasti agasti S. 1. = അഗസ്സ്യന്‍ N. pr. A Rishi celebrated for passing the Vindhya mountains and leading the Brahmans into the Deccan. 2. the star Canopus.
entries.notes: Marked S. (Sanskrit) by Gundert, with the sage-legend intact. No native Malayalam name for Canopus is recorded, though it is a conspicuous southern star from Kerala's latitude.

entries.usage_note: ധ്രുവം കൂട്ടുക is a technical phrase 'to make an astrological calculation'.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ധ്രുവം dhruvam, p. 523
entries.quote: ധ്രുവം dhruvam dhruvam S. ( ധൃ ) 1. Fixed, abiding; sure ... 3. the polar star ധ്രുവത്തിന്‍റെ പേര്‍ ജലജോയം astrol. ധ്രുവം കൂട്ടുക B. to make an astrological calculation. ധ്രുവന്‍ 1. the polar-star, personified
entries.notes: Purely Sanskrit; Gundert records no Dravidian pole-star name for Malayalam. (Thurston, Castes and Tribes of Southern India, vol. I p. 108, records a Dravidian one for the Nilgiri Badagas — 'Aranjoti (the pole-star)', shown to the couple at a wedding — but Badaga is outside this compilation.) The astrological gloss ജലജോയം is obscure.

modern_star.common_name: the seven bright stars of the Big Dipper

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. സപ്തം saptam, p. 1036 (sub-entry സപ്തര്‍ഷികള്‍); the seven are named s.v. ഋഷി, p. 154
entries.quote: സപ്തര്‍ഷികള്‍ Ursa Major (& സപ്ത ഋഷികള്‍ Bhg.)
entries.notes: Gundert's list of the seven under ഋഷി (p. 154) is Kaśyapa, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, Gautama, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja — the Purāṇic set, not the Bṛhat Saṃhitā set used in the Sanskrit database. Sanskrit word with a native Malayalam plural in -kaḷ. No vernacular Malayalam name for the Great Bear turned up in any source searched.

entries.sky_object: the Bear; a constellation in general
entries.usage_note: Used in the compound ജന്മര്‍ക്ഷദിനം 'the day of one's birth-asterism'.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഋക്ഷം ṛkṣam, p. 153
entries.quote: ഋക്ഷം r̥kṣam ṛkšam S. (G. 'rktos) 1. Bear, Ursa minor. 2. constellation in general ജന്മര്‍ക്ഷദി നം Bhg.
entries.notes: Gundert glosses the Bear as Ursa MINOR, where Sanskrit ṛkṣāḥ is standardly Ursa Major (the Saptarṣis) — as Gundert himself has it under സപ്തം. The discrepancy is his, not the language's; flagged disputed. Sense 2, 'constellation in general', is the ordinary Malayalam usage.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ആകാശം ākāśam, p. 70
entries.quote: ആകാശഗംഗ milky way Bhg 5.
entries.notes: Cited from the Malayalam Bhāgavata. Gundert repeats it s.v. ഗം gam, p. 328: 'Also ആകാശ ഗംഗ the milky way.'

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. സുര sura, p. 1060
entries.quote: സുരവാഹിനി the milky way AR.
entries.notes: Cited from Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇam (Malayalam). Not among the Milky Way synonyms collected in the Sanskrit database, which has Suradīrghikā and Svarnadī but not Suravāhinī — a Kerala-side addition to the Sanskrit synonym list.

entries.usage_note: Gundert's citation is about the direction of its rising: 'ധൂ. പടിഞ്ഞാറു ഉദിക്ക' — the comet rises in the west (from Brahmāṇḍapurāṇam), an omen datum.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ധൂമം dhūmam, p. 521
entries.quote: ധൂമകേതു having smoke for a sign (= fire); a comet ധൂ. പടിഞ്ഞാറു ഉദിക്ക Brhmd.
entries.notes: The learned counterpart of വാല്‍മീന്‍. Gundert also records, s.v. വൈദ്യം p. 998, that 'some call a comet വൈധൃതി' — vaidhṛti, otherwise the name of an astrological yoga.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഉല്ക ulka, p. 144
entries.quote: ഉല്ക ulka ulγa S. Meteor, firebrand.
entries.notes: Exactly parallel in sense to native കൊളളിമീന്‍ / കൊളളി — both languages built the meteor word on 'firebrand'.

entries.usage_note: Also the everyday word for a person's birth-star: ജന്മനക്ഷത്രം, 'the asterism under which one is born' (Gundert s.v. ജന്മം, p. 403).
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. നക്ഷത്രം nakṣatram, p. 524
entries.quote: നക്ഷത്രം nakṣatram nakšatram S. ( നക്ഷ് to come up). 1. A star, (vu. നച്ചത്രം, നസ്ക്യേതിരം ), ശൂലാ ഗ്രേ ന'ങ്ങള്‍ എണ്ണിക്കൊള്‍ക PT. 2. a lunar asterism (27 or 28), of which 2¼ are counted upon one month
entries.notes: The vulgar forms Gundert records in parentheses — നച്ചത്രം naccatram and നസ്ക്യേതിരം naskyētiram — are the register point in miniature: the Sanskrit word ground down by ordinary Malayalam mouths. നാള്‍ nāḷ 'day' is the common colloquial substitute for the birth-star.

entries.sky_object: the host of stars; the zodiac
entries.literal_meaning: 'the troop of stars' (ഭം a star + ഗണം troop)
entries.usage_note: A technical term of Kerala astronomy: ഭഗണം also means a complete revolution, and ഭഗണഭൂദിനങ്ങള്‍ 'revolutions and civil days in a caturyuga' is quoted from a Malayalam gaṇita text.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ഭഗണം bhagaṇam, p. 756
entries.quote: ഭഗണം bhagaṇam bhaġaṇam S. ( ഭം a star, fr. ഭാ ). The host of stars, zodiac; also = 1/12 രാശി (astr.). ചതുര്‍യ്യുഗത്തിങ്കലേ ഭഗണഭൂദിനങ്ങള്‍, തികഞ്ഞ ഭ'ങ്ങള്‍ ഉളവാകും Gan.
entries.notes: Gundert's citation 'Gan.' is a Malayalam mathematical/astronomical work — direct lexical evidence that the technical vocabulary of the Kerala school passed into the general language. Note also ഭഗണന്‍ 'an astrologer' in the same entry.

entries.usage_note: Weather proverb: കാര്‍ത്തിക കഴിഞ്ഞാല്‍ മഴയില്ല, 'once Kārttika is past there is no more rain' — the Pleiades period marking the end of the north-east monsoon.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. കാര്‍ത്തിക kārttika, p. 240
entries.quote: കാര്‍ത്തിക kār‍ttika kārtiγa S. ( കൃത്തിക ) The 3d constellation, the Pleiades; the 3rd day of the lunar month. കാര്‍ത്തികം = വൃശ്ചികം Oct. — Nov. കാര്‍ത്തിക ക ഴിഞ്ഞാല്‍ മഴയില്ല prov.
entries.notes: Gundert also records the Sanskrit form കൃത്തിക in Malayalam with the six-nurse legend, s.v. കൃത്തം p. 289: 'കൃത്തിക the 6 Pleiades ആറു കൃ. മാരും മുല നല്കി KR.' — 'the six Kṛttikās gave suck', to Kārttikeya. Malayalam has no attested native counting-name for the cluster of the Tamil aṟumīn 'six stars' type; the proverb is the vernacular layer.

entries.usage_note: Aṣṭamirōhiṇi, the eighth lunar day falling in Rohiṇi in the month Ciṅṅam, is Kṛṣṇa's birthday and a fast day in Kerala.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. രോഹം rōham, p. 889 (sub-entry രോഹിണി)
entries.quote: the 4th Nakšatra, with Aldebaran ചിങ്ങമാം മാസ വും അഷ്ടമിരോ. നാള്‍ Bhg. CG. K/?/šṇa's birthday.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. മകയിരം makayiram, p. 769
entries.quote: മകയിരം makayiram maγairam & മകയിര്യം (S. മൃഗ ശീര്‍ഷം). The 5th constellation, head of Orion. മകീരം മുന്നല്‍ നടന്ന കന്നിയില്‍ (astrol.).
entries.notes: A heavy phonological reshaping of mṛgaśīrṣa — mṛga- → maka-, -śīrṣa → -yiram — with a further contracted form മകീരം makīram quoted from an astrological text. Malayalam thus names Orion's head twice over, here and at ഇന്വകകള്‍.

entries.usage_note: The most socially prominent asterism in Kerala. Tiruvātira in Dhanu is a women's festival of Śiva; the Tiruvātira ñāṟṟu at the start of Mithunam is the planting period at the burst of the south-west monsoon (Gundert s.v. ഞാറു, p. 412).
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ആതിര ātira, p. 79
entries.quote: ആതിര ātira āδira T. M. & തിരുവാതിര (S. ആ ര്‍ദ്രാ ) The 6th Asterism, star in Gemini.
entries.notes: Gundert marks it 'T. M.', i.e. shared Tamil-Malayalam, not a fresh Sanskrit loan; and he places the star in Gemini, where Ārdrā is standardly Betelgeuse in Orion. The Kerala school's own texts put Ārdrā at Betelgeuse, so Gundert's 'Gemini' is treated here as loose — hence 'likely'. Thurston's account of the Nāyars (Castes and Tribes of Southern India, vol. V) heads the festival section 'Tiruvatira or Ardra star', confirming the asterism identification outside the dictionary.

entries.usage_note: Proverbial: മകം പിറന്ന മങ്ക, 'a girl born under Makam' — an auspicious birth.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. മകം makam, p. 769
entries.quote: മകം makam maγam 1. Tdbh. of മഘ . The 10th constellation (Regulus). മകമാം നാളന്നു KR. മകം പിറന്ന മങ്ക prov.
entries.notes: Gundert's 'Tdbh.' (tadbhava) marking is his standard signal that the word has been through Dravidian phonology rather than borrowed whole.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ചിത്ര citra, p. 361
entries.quote: ചിത്ര citra čitra S. (foll.) & ചിത്തിര 1. The 14th lunar asterism (Spica virginis; mod, bright star in Bootes); the month ചൈത്രം or മേടം .
entries.notes: Gundert gives two incompatible identifications in one breath — Spica, and 'mod. bright star in Bootes' (i.e. Arcturus). The second is an error, probably contamination from ചോതി/Svātī on the facing sense; Spica is the standard identification and is what the Sanskrit database carries.

entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. ചോതി cōti, p. 396
entries.quote: ചോതി cō̄taി čōδi 1. Tdbh., സ്വാതി The 15th lunar asterism, Arcturus. 2. Tdbh. ജ്യോതിസ്സ് light പരമചോതി Anj.
entries.notes: Two different Sanskrit words, svāti and jyotis, have fallen together as ചോതി in Malayalam — a good illustration of what tadbhava reduction costs. Gundert confirms the star sense again s.v. സ്വസാ, p. 1074: 'Arcturus, ചോതി.'

entries.usage_note: Tṛkkēṭṭa is one of the inauspicious birth-stars in Kerala reckoning; Gundert lists it under ഗണ്ഡാന്തം (p. 329), the perilous junctions of the asterism cycle.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. കേട്ട kēṭṭa, p. 293
entries.quote: കേട്ട kēṭṭa kēṭṭa തൃക്കേട്ട T. M. (Tdbh., ജ്യേഷ്ഠ; ചേ ട്ട Pandora) The 18th lunar asterism in Scorpion.
entries.notes: Gundert's parenthesis '(ചേട്ട Pandora)' refers to Cēṭṭā/Jyeṣṭhā the goddess of misfortune, whom he likens to Pandora — the asterism and the ill-luck goddess share the name. Gundert gives no separate name for Antares as a star apart from the asterism.

entries.usage_note: Names the national festival of Kerala: Gundert, 'the national feast on new moon of Sept. lasting 10 days, when Paraśurāma is still said to visit Kēraḷa'.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. തിരുന്പുക tirumpuka, p. 459 (sub-entry തിരുവോണം); and s.v. ഓണം ōṇam, p. 184
entries.quote: തിരുവോണം (S. ശ്രവണം ) 1. the 22nd asterism including Aquila (in Cancer V1.). 2. the feast ഓണം in August.
entries.notes: The clearest case in Malayalam of an asterism name outgrowing astronomy: Ōṇam is now first a harvest festival and only second a star. Gundert's ഓണം entry (p. 184) leads with 'The 22nd constellation, Aquila'.

entries.sky_object: the 27 lunar mansions in Malayalam form
entries.name_native: അശ്വതി, ഭരണി, കാര്‍ത്തിക, രോഹിണി, മകയിരം, തിരുവാതിര, പുണര്‍തം, പൂയം, ആയില്യം, മകം, പൂരം, ഉത്രം, അത്തം, ചിത്ര, ചോതി, വിശാഖം, അനുഴം, തൃക്കേട്ട, മൂലം, പൂരാടം, ഉത്രാടം, തിരുവോണം, അവിട്ടം, ചതയം, പൂരുരുട്ടാതി, ഉത്രട്ടാതി, ഇരവതി
entries.name_roman: aśvati, bharaṇi, kārttika, rōhiṇi, makayiram, tiruvātira, puṇartam, pūyam, āyilyam, makam, pūram, utram, attam, citra, cōti, viśākham, anuḻam, tṛkkēṭṭa, mūlam, pūrāṭam, utrāṭam, tiruvōṇam, aviṭṭam, catayam, pūruruṭṭāti, utraṭṭāti, iravati
entries.usage_note: Malayalam uses the full 27-nakshatra series and it still governs birth-star reckoning, name-giving, marriage-matching and festival dates. Gundert's ജന്മനക്ഷത്രം is 'the asterism, under which one is born' (p. 403), and അനുജന്മനക്ഷത്രം 'the 10th and 19th asterisms after the ജന്മനക്ഷത്രം' (p. 28) shows the derived reckoning already lexicalised in 1872.
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.vv. അശ്വതി p. 64, ഭരം (ഭരണി) p. 759, കാര്‍ത്തിക p. 240, രോഹം (രോഹിണി) p. 889, മകയിരം p. 769, ആതിര p. 79, പുണര്‍ (പുണര്‍തം) p. 673, ആയിലിയം p. 85, മകം p. 769, ഉത്രം (also ഉത്രാടം, ഉത്രട്ടാതി) p. 129, അത്തം p. 22, ചിത്ര p. 361, ചോതി p. 396, വിശരി (വിശാഖ) p. 961, അനുഴം p. 27, കേട്ട p. 293, മൂലം p. 853, പൂരണം (പൂരാടം) p. 693, ഓണം p. 184 / തിരുവോണം p. 459, അവിട്ടം p. 62, ചതയം p. 343, ഇരവതി p. 109
entries.quote: നക്ഷത്രം ... 2. a lunar asterism (27 or 28), of which 2¼ are counted upon one month
entries.notes: Recorded as one entry, deliberately, because these are the Sanskrit names in Malayalam phonology and are not the point of this compilation. Gundert marks most of them 'Tdbh.' (tadbhava) and several 'T. M.' (common Tamil-Malayalam), i.e. inherited through the southern tradition rather than freshly borrowed: അത്തം < hasta, ഇരവതി < revatī, ഓണം < śrāvaṇa, ചോതി < svātī, ചതയം < śatabhiṣaj, അവിട്ടം < śraviṣṭhā, മകം < maghā, അനുഴം < anurādhā. Gundert's star identifications, where he gives them, are mostly the standard ones; two are odd — അത്തം 'Coma Berenices' (p. 22; Hasta is standardly in Corvus) and അനുഴം 'Lupus and scorpion's head' (p. 27) — and should not be relied on.

entries.usage_note: Ethnographic confirmation that the asterism, not merely the festival name, is what Kerala reckons by: Thurston lists it among the Nambūtiri Brahman observances of the year, fixed to the month of Dhanu, preceded by seven days of pre-dawn bathing and kept as a night vigil by husband and wife.
entries.citation: Thurston & Rangachari, Castes and Tribes of Southern India (Madras, 1909), vol. V, s.v. Nambutiri Brahman, pp. 194–195
entries.quote: (5) Tiruvatira or Ardra star. — In the month of Dhanu. This is a day of universal festivity and rejoicing.
entries.notes: Thurston romanizes only; no Malayalam script is printed, so name_native is left null. Across all seven volumes of Thurston, searched electronically, no Malayalam vernacular star name appears at all: the words Pleiades, Orion, Canopus, Sirius, Arcturus, pole star and Milky Way do not occur once in the whole work.

entries.usage_note: The everyday Malayalam word for a person's birth-star, and the one that does the social work: Gundert's illustrative phrase is നാളും പൊരുത്തവും നോക്കി നിശ്ചയിക്ക, 'to settle [a marriage] after examining the nāḷ and the compatibility'. He also records the classification of the asterisms as ആണ്‍നാള്‍ 'male nāḷ' and പെണ്‍നാള്‍ 'female nāḷ' (cf. s.v. പെണ്‍, p. 699), and മുന്നാള്‍ 'the 3rd asterism from that of the nativity' (s.v. മുന്‍, p. 837).
entries.citation: Gundert, A Malayalam and English Dictionary (1872), s.v. നാള്‍ nāḷ, p. 547 (sense 2)
entries.quote: നാള്‍ nāḷ‍ nāḷ T. M. ... 1. A day of 24 hours ... 2. the astrological day & the നക്ഷത്രം that governs it ( ആണ്‍നാ., പെണ്‍നാ . etc.). നാളും പൊരുത്ത വും നോക്കി നിശ്ചയിക്ക Anach. (for marriage).
entries.notes: The register point of the whole Malayalam set: the twenty-seven asterisms are Sanskrit, but the word Malayalam actually uses for them in daily speech is the inherited Dravidian nāḷ 'day' — the same word as Tamil nāḷ. Sanskrit നക്ഷത്രം is the learned register; നാള്‍ is the lived one. Gundert marks it 'T. M.' with Kannada and Telugu cognates.

entries.usage_note: The ordinary Tulu word for a star; also 'silver', 'three annas' and 'a gray ox'.
entries.citation: Männer, Tuḷu–English Dictionary (Mangalore, Basel Mission Press, 1886), s.v. ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ boḷḷi, p. 502
entries.quote: ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ bolli, s. A star. 2. silver. 3. three annas. 4. a gray ox. —ನೂಲು silver thread or girdle.
entries.notes: THE Tulu star-word, and the only native one. Burrow & Emeneau confirm it independently at DEDR 5496(a), whose Tulu section lists boḷḷi in the senses 'star, silver' among the reflexes of *veḷ 'white' (DSAL p. 499). The cognate set — Ta. veḷḷi 'silver, star, planet Venus, Friday', Ka. beḷḷi 'silver, planet Venus', To. piḷy, Ko. veyḷ, Ma. വെള്ളി — makes 'silver / Venus / Friday' a single inherited Dravidian complex, and Tulu belongs to it. Männer's romanization is 'bolli'; the printed Kannada script has the retroflex ḷ. The OCR of the Kannada in Männer is unusable, so the script here was read from the page image.

entries.literal_meaning: 'the star of evening' (ತಂಜ tanja 'evening, sunset, night' + genitive -ದ -da + ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ boḷḷi 'star')
entries.citation: Männer, Tuḷu–English Dictionary (1886), s.v. ತಂಜ tanja, p. 262 (sub-entry)
entries.quote: ತಂಜ tanja, s. Evening, sunset, night. —ದ ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ the evening star.
entries.notes: Read directly from the page scan of p. 262; Männer's dash convention repeats the headword, so the full compound is ತಂಜದ ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ. Wholly native. Note the split with Kodava: Tulu lexicalises Venus as the EVENING star, Kodagu as the MORNING star, both on the same *veḷ root. Männer's Tulu→English volume has no entry for 'morning star' at all.

modern_star.common_name: the seven bright stars of the Big Dipper

entries.literal_meaning: 'the star-cluster of the cot' — ಹೊರಸು horasu 'a cot, a couch' (Kittel, Kannada-English Dictionary, p. 1771) + genitive + ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ nakṣatra 'star' + ಕೂಟ kūṭa 'assembly, cluster'
entries.citation: Männer, English–Tuḷu Dictionary (Basel Mission Press, 1888), s.v. Ursa, p. 617
entries.quote: Ursa, ಕರೊಡಿ; —major ಹೊರಸಿನ್ಟ ನಕ್ಷತ್ರೊಳಿ ಕೂಟ, ಸಪ್ತರ್ಷಿಗಳು.
entries.notes: The one indigenous constellation IMAGE recovered for either Tulu or Kodava: the Big Dipper seen as a cot or bedstead, not as a bear and not as seven sages. Männer's first gloss ಕರೊಡಿ karoḍi is simply the animal 'bear', and his alternative ಸಪ್ತರ್ಷಿಗಳು saptarṣigaḷu is the Sanskrit 'Seven Ṛṣis'. TRANSLITERATION CAVEAT: the conjunct in ಹೊರಸಿನ್_ is not fully legible even at 2400px — the subscript could be ṭa or sa — so the genitive is given as -nṭa on morphological grounds and the reading should be checked against the printed book. Note also that horasu is not a headword in Männer's Tulu→English direction, so the word is printed here but nowhere defined by him.

entries.literal_meaning: 'row/line of stars' (ಸಾಲ್ sāl 'row, line', native Dravidian)
entries.citation: Männer, English–Tuḷu Dictionary (1888), s.v. Galaxy, p. 208
entries.quote: Galaxy, s. ಆಕಾಶಗಂಗೆ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರೊಳಿ ಸಾಲ್.
entries.notes: A descriptive Tulu phrase set beside the Sanskrit ಆಕಾಶಗಂಗೆ ākāśagaṅge 'sky-Ganges' — the same compound Malayalam and Sinhala both have. Marked 'likely' because a lexicographer's English-to-Tulu equivalent may be his own rendering rather than a current name; Männer gives no citation or usage. Only the second element is Sanskrit.

entries.citation: Männer, Tuḷu–English Dictionary (1886), s.v. ಬಾಲನಕ್ಷತ್ರ bālanakṣatra, p. 481
entries.quote: ಬಾಲನಕ್ಷತ್ರ balanakṣatra, s. A comet.
entries.notes: Hybrid on the Malayalam വാല്‍നക്ഷത്രം pattern: native 'tail' plus Sanskrit nakṣatra. Männer's English→Tulu volume gives the same word (spelt ಬೀಲನಕ್ಷತ್ರ, p. 75) alongside Sanskrit ಧೂಮಕೇತು dhūmakētu, which he also carries under ಧೂಮ 'smoke' (Tulu→English p. 337). Marked 'likely' on the transliteration, which comes from a garbled OCR line confirmed only in outline against the page.

entries.literal_meaning: 'the stone that fell from the sky'
entries.citation: Männer, English–Tuḷu Dictionary (1888), s.v. Meteorite, p. 327
entries.quote: Meteorite, Meteorolite, s. ಆಕಾಶೊಡ್ಡು ಬೂರ್ದಿ ಕಲ್ಲ್.
entries.notes: A descriptive Tulu phrase rather than a name — everything but ಆಕಾಶ ākāśa 'sky' is native. Compare the Sinhala තරුගල tarugala 'star-stone', which is also only a gloss and not a headword. Männer's word for the phenomenon itself is Sanskrit: ಉಲ್ಕಾಪಾತ ulkāpāta, 'The falling of meteors, which is considered a bad sign. 2. an omen' (Tulu→English p. 74).

entries.citation: Männer, Tuḷu–English Dictionary (1886), s.v. ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ nakṣatra, p. 348
entries.quote: ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ nakṣatra, s. A star, planet. 2. a constellation or lunar mansion.
entries.notes: Tulu takes the whole learned apparatus straight from Sanskrit as tatsamas, without the Eḷu-style phonological reshaping Sinhala applies or the tadbhava reduction Malayalam applies: ತಾರ tāra (p. 278), ಉಡು uḍu (p. 67), ಜ್ಯೋತಿ jyoti (p. 255), ಕೃತಿಕೆ kṛtikè 'the Pleiades' (p. 157), ಮೃಗಶಿರ mṛgaśira 'head of Orion' (p. 560), ಸ್ವಾತಿ svāti 'Arcturus' (p. 668), ಶುಕ್ರ śukra 'Venus' (p. 618), ಧ್ರುವನಕ್ಷತ್ರ dhruvanakṣatra 'pole star' (English→Tulu p. 406), and the individual nakṣatra names. Männer's 'Star' entry in the English→Tulu volume (p. 537) heads the list with native ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ boḷḷi and then gives ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ, ತಾರ, ಉಡು.

entries.sky_object: the twelve solar months of the agricultural year
entries.name_roman: Paggu, Besha, Kártél, Áte, Sóna, Nirnala, Bóntel, Járde, Perárde, Puyintél, Máyi, Suggi
entries.usage_note: These, and not any star, are what Tulu cultivation runs on: Sturrock states that all the operations of cultivation are regulated by the solar months, which alone are well known to the cultivating classes in Tuluva proper, while written leases follow the lunar reckoning because they are drawn up in Kannada by Brahmins.
entries.citation: Sturrock, Madras District Manuals: South Canara, vol. I (Madras, 1894), p. 216
entries.quote: …there are Tulu names for the solar, but not for the luni-solar months, thus— Sanskrit. Tulu. Mésha. Paggu. Vrishabha. Besha. Mithuna. Kártél. Karkataca. Áte. Sinha. Sóna. Kanya. Nirnala. Tulá. Bóntel. Vrischika. Járde. Dhanus. Perárde. Makara. Puyintél. Kumbha. Máyi. Mína. Suggi.
entries.notes: Included because it is the negative answer to the agricultural-star question for Tulu, stated positively. Where Malayalam divides the year by twenty-seven asterism-periods (ñāṟṟuveḷa) and names each after a star, Tulu divides it by twelve solar months with wholly native names that are not star-names at all. Sturrock romanizes only; no Kannada script is printed, so name_native is null. The quote is from the archive.org OCR and its accents are as OCR'd.

entries.literal_meaning: 'silver star' / 'white star' — boḷḷi 'silver' (< Dravidian *veḷ 'white') + mi·nï 'star' (< Dravidian *mīn)
entries.citation: Burrow & Emeneau, A Dravidian Etymological Dictionary, entry 5496(a), Kodagu section (DSAL p. 499)
entries.quote: Koḍ. ... boḷḷi silver ... boḷḷi mi·nï morning star
entries.notes: The single most valuable Kodava find: a fully native Dravidian name for Venus, built from two inherited roots. It is also the ONLY place in DEDR where Kodagu mi·nï 'star' appears at all — DEDR 4876, the *mīn entry, gives Kodagu only 'minn- to lighten, flicker' and gives Tulu no star word whatever, though it gives 'Ma. mīn star' and 'Ta. mīṉ star'. So Kodagu has kept the ancient Dravidian word for star only inside this one compound. DEDR romanizes only; no script is printed, so name_native is null. Burrow & Emeneau's 2nd edition (1984) is in copyright; the entry is quoted here as raw lexical data, minimally, for attestation.

entries.usage_note: The Kodava weekday name, in a list where Sunday and Monday are likewise built on native words for sun and moon while Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday are Sanskrit planet-names.
entries.citation: Cole, An Elementary Grammar of the Coorg Language (Bangalore, 1867), 'Days', p. 136
entries.quote: ನಾರಾಚೆ nárắche, Sunday. ತಿಂಗಳಾಚೆ tingaḷáche, Monday. ಚೊವುಳಚೆ chovuáche, Tuesday. ಪೊದನಾಚೆ podanáche, Wednesday. ಬೇಳಾಚೆ béḷáche, Thursday. ಬೊಳ್ಳಿಳಾಚೆ boḷḷiáche, Friday. ಚನಿಳಚೆ chaniáche, Saturday.
entries.notes: Cole glosses the first two names himself — nárắche from nárayaṇa 'a name of the deity used also for the sun', tingaḷáche from tingaḷu 'the moon' — but does not gloss boḷḷi; the Venus sense comes from DEDR 5496, where every close cognate (Ta. veḷḷi, Ka. beḷḷi, To. piḷy, Ko. veyḷ) means 'silver, Venus, Friday' together. Marked 'likely' for that inferential step and because the OCR of Cole's Kannada is poor: the romanizations are Cole's own, the script as reconstructed from the scan. Cole's grammar contains NO Kodava word for 'star' anywhere, including its vocabulary (pp. 51–71).

entries.sky_object: an invisible star or constellation receiving household sacrifice
entries.usage_note: Every Coorg house owed it an annual sacrifice — fowls, coconuts and a little brandy at a stone laid at the foot of a tree with milky juice. A second Gulika, Mṛtyu Gulika 'the Gulika of death', was worshipped where deaths in a family were frequent.
entries.citation: Rice, Mysore and Coorg: A Gazetteer, vol. III (Bangalore, 1878), 'Gulika', p. 263; also Richter, Gazetteer of Coorg (1870), pp. 165–167
entries.quote: This is an invisible constellation or star, belonging both to the order of planets and to that of the zodiacal stars. It is, as the people say, a son of S'ani or Saturn. No mortal eye sees it. The astrologer only knows the Gulika and its power, especially over the sick.
entries.notes: Unidentified by definition — the sources insist the object is invisible. The name is the Sanskrit astrological Gulika (Māndi), the shadowy 'son of Saturn' of Indian horoscopy, so the word is a loan; what is Coorg-specific is that it received a household blood sacrifice at a stone under a tree. Included as the only Kodava sky-cult recorded in the public-domain gazetteers. Richter's independent testimony that Coorg horoscopy at marriage was 'evidently an innovation' suggests this cult sat outside, and predated, the Brahmanical astrology later grafted on.

entries.literal_meaning: 'seven-produced' — හත් hat 'seven' (the inherited numeral, beside Sanskritic සත්) + දින්න, which Carter derives from දිනි 'produced'
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. හත්·දින්න hat·dinna, p. 713
entries.quote: හත්·දින්න hat·dinna , n. (දින්න fr. දිනි produced), the const. Pleiads. Pleiades, කැතිනැකත.
entries.notes: The single clearest case in Sinhala of a sky-object that got a native name rather than a loan — and Carter parses it for us, so the etymology is the source's, not the compiler's. It coexists with the Eḷu loan කැති නැකත, to which Carter cross-refers it in both directions (p. 169, p. 713), and with the Sanskrit tatsama කෘත්තිකා (p. 182). Clough 1892 has it too, without gloss beyond the identification: 'Haddinna, s. the Pleiades' (p. 723). Jayatilaka cross-refers to it from ක්‍රිටික kriṭika, 'N. given to seven stars in the constellation Taurus; Pleiades', p. 3497.

entries.usage_note: Attested in the classical poem Sasadāvata: the rising of this star is what makes turbid water run clear. That belief — Agastya's heliacal rising as the moment water purifies — is the same one Sanskrit attaches to Agastya, but here it is carried by a Sinhala word.
entries.citation: Jayatilaka (ed.), A Dictionary of the Sinhalese Language (Royal Asiatic Society, Ceylon Branch, 1935– ), s.v. කළමුනිදුතරුව kaḷamunin̆du-taruva, p. 2536
entries.quote: කළමුනිදුතරුව kaḷamunin̆du-taruva , s., a brilliant star that dawns in the southern sky, the star canopus of which the sage Agasti is supposed to be the regent: vimal kärä sihil kaḷamunin̆du taru nän̆gīmen by the rising of the star canopus making water purified, Sas 82.
entries.notes: A Jayatilaka-only find; Carter has no such headword and gives only the Sanskrit personal name (අගස්ති, p. 6: 'a rishi so named ... is the regent of the star Canopus'), as does Clough. The final element තරුව taruva is the native Sinhala word for star. Jayatilaka's separate entry අගති agati (p. 41) records the water-purifying belief again.

entries.usage_note: Carter attaches the Kailāsa origin-myth to it; Clough glosses it only 'the celestial river' and does not connect it to the galaxy at all.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. අහස් ගඟ ahas gan̆ga, p. 84
entries.quote: අහස් ගඟ ahas gan̆ga , n. celestial river, supposed to issue from the foot of mount කෛලාස; the milky-way.
entries.notes: Native in form, borrowed in concept: both morphemes are ordinary Sinhala, but Jayatilaka's etymology bracket at අහස්ගඟ (p. 978) reads '[Cf. P. ākāsa-gaṅgā, Sk. ākāśa-gaṅgā]', so it is a morpheme-for-morpheme calque of the Pali/Sanskrit compound — exactly the same compound the Malayalam ആകാശഗംഗ takes over unchanged. Sinhala translated it; Malayalam borrowed it. Carter's synonym list, all loans or hybrids, is අඹුරු නිය am̆buru niya (p. 58), නාග·විථිය nāga·vithiya (p. 319, 'the path of Indra's elephant Airāvata'), බාරුසීගඟ bārusīgan̆ga (p. 446), මන්‍දා·කිනිය man‍dā·kiniya (p. 479), සුර·සිඳුව sura·sin̆duva (p. 692) and ස්වර්නදිය svarnadiya (p. 711).

entries.literal_meaning: 'star after sunset' — Jayatilaka's own gloss; ඉරබටු ira-baṭu 'sunset' from ඉර ira, the inherited Sinhala word for the sun
entries.citation: Jayatilaka (ed.), A Dictionary of the Sinhalese Language (Royal Asiatic Society, Ceylon Branch, 1935– ), s.v. ඉරබටු තරුව irabaṭu-taruva, p. 1505
entries.quote: ඉරබටු තරුව irabaṭu1-taruva , s., (lit. star after sunset) evening star, planet Venus: LṃkVrṇ 2-9; Sāmdrkś 13-24; Ākāś 17-15; MāBhū 4-10.
entries.notes: Wholly native. Carter has it only as the Sinhala gloss inside Sanskrit headwords — පශ්චිම·තරුව paścima·taruva 'evening star, ඉරබටු තාරකාව' (p. 368) and සන්‍ධ්‍යා·තාරකාව (p. 648) — and prints the variant හිර·බටු hira·baṭu, 'sunset, as හිරබටුතරුව, sunset star, evening star' (p. 724). Sinhala therefore lexicalises the morning and evening apparitions separately with two native compounds, as Malayalam does with പെരുമീന്‍/കൊററി.

entries.literal_meaning: 'dawn-star' — Carter's adjacent headword is 'පහන් pahan , a. pert. to light or morning' (p. 371)
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. පහන් තරුව pahan taruva, p. 371
entries.quote: පහන් තරුව, පහන්·තාරකාව pahan taruva, pahan·tārakāva , n. morning star, Venus, Lucifer, සිකුරුතරුව.
entries.notes: The doublet පහන් තරුව / පහන් තාරකාව shows the two registers side by side in one headword: native තරුව taruva against Sanskrit තාරකා tārakā. Jayatilaka attests the native form in running text s.v. අස්තඞ්ගමය (p. 947).

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. දවහත්·තරුව davahat·taruva, p. 278
entries.quote: දවහත්·තරුව davahat·taruva , n. day-star, morning star, Venus, පහන්තාරකාව.
entries.notes: Carter makes it the morning star; Jayatilaka quotes it in a classical simile as the EVENING star — 'tārā-gaṇayan kerehi arundhatī davahat-taru sē diliyeyi', s.v. අරුන්දති, p. 641. Clough (p. 236) lists it with no gloss at all: 'Dawahat-taruwa, s. star so called.' The word is certainly attested and certainly native; which apparition of Venus it names is not settled by the sources, hence 'disputed'.

entries.literal_meaning: 'smoke-banner' (දුම් dum 'smoke' + කෙහෙලි keheli 'banner, trophy of victory')
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. දුම්·කෙහෙලිය dum·keheliya, p. 292
entries.quote: දුම්·කෙහෙලිය dum·keheliya , n. comet, වල්ගාතරුව; fire, ගින්න.
entries.notes: A morpheme-for-morpheme Sinhala rendering of Sanskrit dhūma-ketu 'smoke-bannered', which Carter also carries unchanged as ධූම·කේතුව (p. 311). The same word in two registers on facing pages. Carter's cross-reference here uses the fully native වල්ගාතරුව valgā-taruva, while his own headword at p. 568 is the hybrid වල්ගා·තාරකාව valgā·tārakāva, 'tailed-star, viz. comet'.

entries.usage_note: Compounds: උළු කැන uḷu kæna 'cluster of stars, constellation' (p. 130); උළිඳු uḷin̆du and උළු රජ uḷu raja, which Carter parses as 'උළු star, ඉඳු lord' — 'Star-lord, Star-king', an epithet of the moon (p. 130).
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. උළු uḷu, p. 130
entries.quote: උළු uḷu , n . tiles; star.
entries.notes: An old native word for 'star', productive in poetic compounds but displaced in ordinary use by තරුව taruva and the Eḷu loan නැකත nækata.

entries.usage_note: The productive native element in the Sinhala sky vocabulary: පහන් තරුව morning star, ඉරබටු තරුව evening star, කළමුනිදුතරුව Canopus, වල්ගාතරුව comet, තරුගල 'star-stone' meteorite.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. තරුව taruva, p. 253
entries.quote: තරුව taruva , n. tree, ගහ; star, තාරකාව; pupil of the eye, කළු ඉංගිරියාව; pl. තරු.
entries.notes: Sinhala's answer to Malayalam മീന്‍: the inherited word that does the compounding work while the Sanskrit synonym තාරකා tārakā stays learned. Carter's native constellation words are built on it — තරු·වැළ taru·væḷa 'cluster or string of stars, constellation' and තරු·පොකුර taru·pokura 'cluster of stars, asterism' (both p. 253).

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. තරු·වැළ taru·væḷa, p. 253
entries.quote: තරු·වැළ taru·væḷa , n. cluster or string of stars, constellaion.
entries.notes: 'constellaion' as printed. Beside it Carter has තරු·පොකුර taru·pokura 'cluster of stars, asterism' and the native උළු කැන uḷu kæna, against the Sanskrit තාරකා·පංක්තිය tārakā·paṅktiya (p. 256). Sinhala thus has three native words for 'constellation' where Malayalam has none and must use നക്ഷത്രം.

entries.usage_note: A festival at the full moon of Il (October–November) — the month in which the full moon stands near the Pleiades. Clough spells out the astronomy: 'when the moon is full near the Pleiades in the month ඉල් මස il-masa, (October-November)'.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. නැකැත්·කෙළිය nækæt·keḷiya, p. 322; Clough, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (1892), s.v. Nakat-keliya, p. 273
entries.quote: නැකැත්·කෙළිය nækæt·keḷiya , n. lit. star-play: a festival observed at full moon in ඉල්මස (Oct.-Nov.).
entries.notes: The folk layer: an asterism doing calendrical work in village life rather than in an almanac. Structurally the counterpart of the Malayalam Tiruvātira and of the Kārttika full-moon reckoning; Jayatilaka's කාර්ත්තිකමාසය (p. 2916) makes the same Pleiades-full-moon definition for the month.

entries.literal_meaning: 'deer's head' — Clough parses it, 'මුව and සිරස head'
entries.citation: Clough, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1892), s.v. Muwa-sirasa, p. 493
entries.quote: Muwa-sirasa, s. (මුව and සිරස head) fifth lunar asterism, figured by the head of a deer; Elu form of මෘගශිරස mriga-siras, which see.
entries.notes: Half-translated rather than merely sound-shifted: the first element මුව muva 'deer' is inherited Sinhala (Clough p. 492: 'Muwa, s. deer ... Elu form of'), the second සිරස sirasa is Sanskrit śiras. Clough's own tag is 'Elu form', so it is filed here as sanskritic, but it is the nearest the nakshatra list comes to a native re-coinage. Clough's djvu.txt OCR of the Sinhala script is unusable, so name_native is left null: only Clough's romanization is recorded. Carter uses the same word inside definitions (ආග්‍රහායර්‍ණය, p. 87, 'the const. Orion, මුවසිරස') but does not carry it as a headword.

entries.usage_note: The everyday Sinhala word for the asterisms and for astrological time-reckoning generally; it is what the almanac and the nekatiyā (astrologer) work with.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. නැකත nækata, p. 322
entries.quote: නැකත nækata , n. star, තරුව; planet, ග්‍රහතාරකාව; lunar mansion or asterism in the moon's path: see නක්‍ෂත්‍රය.
entries.notes: The Eḷu (Sinhala-phonology) reflex of Sanskrit nakṣatra / Pali nakkhatta, beside the learned tatsama නක්‍ෂත්‍රය nakṣatraya (p. 312). Exactly parallel to Malayalam നക്ഷത്രം ~ vulgar നച്ചത്രം. Clough p. 305: 'Nekata, s. star in general, planet; asterism in the moon's path or lunar mansion, of which twenty eight distinct in name, figure, and number, are enumerated in Sinhalese astronomy.'

entries.usage_note: The ordinary name of the third asterism, and the one that fixes the month Il: Jayatilaka quotes 'käti-nakat lada hil-masa', 'in the month of il when the constellation Pleiades has dawned'.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. කැති නැකත kæti nækata, p. 169; and Jayatilaka (ed.), A Dictionary of the Sinhalese Language (Royal Asiatic Society, Ceylon Branch, 1935– ), s.v. කැතිනකත käti-nakata, p. 2994
entries.quote: (astro.) N. of one of the twenty-seven asterisms; constellation Pleiades: AbhdhSn 62 (p. 10); Ruv 635 ... [Cf. Sk. kṛttikā + nakṣatra.]
entries.notes: Jayatilaka's etymology bracket settles the register: kṛttikā + nakṣatra, both loans, in Sinhala phonology. A trap to avoid: කැති kæti is separately the plural of කැත්ත 'billhook' (Carter p. 168), so the compound is homophonous with 'billhook asterism'; no source proposes that etymology and it should not be recorded as a literal meaning.

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. බහුලාව bahulāva, p. 444
entries.quote: බහුලාව bahulāva , n. indigo, නිල් අවරි; cardamoms, එන් සාල් Pleiades, කැතිනැකත.
entries.notes: Sanskrit Bahulā, which the Sanskrit database carries as an Amarakośa synonym of Kṛttikā; Sinhala kept it, with the same indigo/cardamom homonyms Sanskrit has. Clough p. 418 likewise: 'Bahulá, s. indigo ... Pleiades; cow.'

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. ධ්‍රැව·තාරකාව dh‍ræva·tārakāva, p. 312
entries.quote: ධ්‍රැව·තාරකාව dh‍ræva·tārakāva , n. the pole star.
entries.notes: Sinhala kept the Sanskrit word entire and coined nothing native for the pole star — the same result as Malayalam ധ്രുവം. Carter's other pole-star names are all Sanskrit too: ධ්‍රැවය (p. 312), උත්තර ධ්‍රැව තාරකාව (p. 117), ග්‍රහා·ධාරයා 'sustainer of the planets and stars' (p. 222), ජ්‍යෝතී·රථය (p. 245), නක්‍ෂත්‍ර·නාභිය 'star-navel' (p. 312). Clough p. 272 has 'Druwa, s. polar star or north pole itself'. A search for a native form returned nothing in any of the three dictionaries.

modern_star.common_name: the seven bright stars of the Big Dipper

entries.usage_note: The living Sinhala reference to the Dipper is to the seven sages, not to a bear.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. ඍෂියා r̥ṣiyā, p. 132
entries.quote: ඍෂියා r̥ṣiyā , n. H. saint or sage, sp. one of seven of exalted rank; in ast. the seven form the const. Ursa Major.
entries.notes: The bear names in Carter are not vernacular at all but his own English-to-Sinhalese calques, and he flags them: සප්තර්ෂිය saptarṣiya 'const. Ursa Major, see Ursa, E. S.' (p. 651) and සප්ත·මූනී·චාරය 'Charles's-wain. E. S.' (p. 651), where 'E. S.' means Carter is citing his own English-Sinhalese volume. මහා·භල්ලී·රාශිය 'great bear' (p. 487) and ක්‍ෂුද්‍ර භල්ලී රාශිය 'ursa minor' (p. 195) are Sanskrit-built calques of the English. Carter also has චිත්‍ර·ශඛණ්‍ඩිනයෝ (p. 232), 'seven sages, represented by the seven stars of the Great Bear' — the Citraśikhaṇḍinaḥ of the Sanskrit database.

entries.usage_note: Invoked by the bridegroom at marriage as the model wife (Carter, p. 61).
entries.citation: Jayatilaka (ed.), A Dictionary of the Sinhalese Language (Royal Asiatic Society, Ceylon Branch, 1935– ), s.v. අරුන්දති arundati, p. 641
entries.quote: [Slw. P. Sk. arundhatī.]
entries.notes: Jayatilaka identifies the star modernly — Arundhatī as Alcor, and අරුන්ධතීනාථ arundhatī-nātha, 'the husband of Arundhatī, i.e. Vasiṣṭha', as Mizar (both p. 641). This matches the Sanskrit database exactly. WARNING for anyone using Carter: at p. 61 he glosses Arundhatī as 'Pleiades, හත්දින්න, (or one of the stars thereof)', which is wrong; Jayatilaka corrects it. Only the etymology bracket is quoted here because the surrounding Jayatilaka text is a long citation apparatus.

entries.usage_note: The intercalated 28th asterism, squeezed between the 21st and 22nd.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. අභි ජිත් abhi jit, p. 50
entries.quote: අභි ජිත් abhi jit , n. a lunar asterism or three stars between the 21st and 22nd lunar asterisms.
entries.notes: Sinhala inherited the 27/28 ambiguity along with the system: Carter's own නක්‍ෂත්‍රය entry speaks of 28 asterisms (p. 312) and Clough of 'twenty-eight in the moon's path' (p. 273), while the enumerated Eḷu list runs to 27. Jayatilaka makes the identification explicit at අබිජිත් abijit (p. 462), 'this is identified with vēgā, the brightest star in the constellation'.

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. ස්වාති svāti, p. 711
entries.quote: ස්වාති svāti , n. (සු well, අත් to go constantly), the star Arcturus, which is the fifteenth lunar asterism.
entries.notes: Carter's parenthetical parse is a Sanskrit folk-etymology, not Sinhala morphology. The Eḷu form is සාය sāya (p. 673), which Carter glosses first as 'evening' and then as 'the star Arcturus'; Clough has the same double sense at 'Sá' (p. 675). Jayatilaka has no Arcturus entry.

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. දෙට, දෙටු deṭa, deṭu, p. 297
entries.quote: දෙට, දෙටු deṭa, deṭu , a . E. of ජ්‍යේෂ්ඨ .
entries.notes: Carter's 'E. of' = 'Eḷu form of' (verified against Carter's own abbreviation key), i.e. Sanskrit jyeṣṭha in Sinhala phonology. Clough anchors the asterism to the sky: 'Jyeshthá ... the eighteenth, comprising three stars of which one is [α] Scorpionis figured by a ring or earring' (p. 196). Antares itself has no independent Sinhala name — Jayatilaka's only entry is the twentieth-century English loanword අන්ටරේස් anṭarēs, '[lw. Eng. Antares]' (p. 317).

entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. උල්කාව ulkāva, p. 128; Jayatilaka (ed.), A Dictionary of the Sinhalese Language (Royal Asiatic Society, Ceylon Branch, 1935– ), s.v. උල්කාව ulkāva, p. 1909
entries.quote: උල්කාව ulkāva , n. flame, firebrand, විලක්කුව, උල්පන් දම; meteor.
entries.notes: Sanskrit ulkā, the same word Malayalam has as ഉല്ക, and with the same 'firebrand' base sense. The native counterpart survives only as a gloss, not a headword: Carter's උල්කා ගල 'meteorite' (p. 128) is glossed with Sinhala තරුගල tarugala, literally 'star-stone', which is not itself a Carter headword. Carter also records the omen term දික්·හදාය dik·hadāya, 'fiery meteor, regarded as one of the five evil omens of the sky' (p. 284).

entries.literal_meaning: 'the dog star' (Sanskrit sārameya 'canine, son of Saramā')
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.v. සාරමේය·තාරකාව sāramēya·tārakāva, p. 674
entries.quote: සාරමේය·තාරකාව sāramēya·tārakāva , n. dog star, Sirius, ඒ නම්වූ තරුව.
entries.notes: Recorded as a negative in disguise. Carter's Sinhala gloss ඒ නම්වූ තරුව means 'the star of that name' — he had no Sinhala word to give, so he coined a Sanskrit calque of the English 'dog star' and admitted as much in the gloss. Jayatilaka returns 'No results' for Sirius, and the word Sirius does not occur once in Clough 1892. There is no attested vernacular Sinhala name for the brightest star in the sky.

entries.sky_object: the 27 lunar mansions in Sinhala (Eḷu) form
entries.name_native: අස්විද, බෙරණය, කැති නැකත, රෙහෙණ, මුවසිරස, අදේ, පුනාවස, පුසේ·නැකත, අස්ලිස, මා·නැකත, පුවපල්, උතුරුපල්ගුන, හත, සිත, සාය, විසා·නැකත, අනුර, දෙට, මුළ, පුව·සළ, උතුරු සළය, සුවණය, දෙනට, සිය·වස, පුවපුටුපේ, උතුරු පුටුපය, රේවතිය
entries.name_roman: asvida, beraṇaya, kæti nækata, reheṇa, muvasirasa, adē, punāvasa, pusē-nækata, aslisa, mā-nækata, puvapal, uturupalguna, hata, sita, sāya, visā-nækata, anura, deṭa, muḷa, puva-saḷa, uturu saḷaya, suvaṇaya, denaṭa, siya-vasa, puvapuṭupē, uturu puṭupaya, rēvatiya
entries.usage_note: These are the working names of the Sinhala almanac and of nekata reckoning — the choice of auspicious moments that still governs Sri Lankan New Year observances, first ploughing, and the naming of children.
entries.citation: Carter, A Sinhalese-English Dictionary (Colombo, 1924), s.vv. අස්විද p. 84, බෙරණය p. 454, කැති නැකත p. 169, රෙහෙණ p. 542, අදේ p. 25, පුසේ·නැකත p. 400, අස්ලිස p. 83, මා·නැකත p. 491, උතුරුපල්ගුන p. 116, හත p. 713, සාය p. 673, විසා·නැකත p. 604, අනුර p. 37, දෙට p. 297, මුළ p. 507, පුව·සළ p. 399, උතුරු සළය p. 117, සුවණය p. 694, දෙනට p. 297, සිය·වස p. 682, පුවපුටුපේ p. 399, උතුරු පුටුපය p. 116, රේවතිය p. 542; Clough (1892) s.vv. Muwa-sirasa p. 493, Punáwasa p. 364, Puwapal p. 368
entries.quote: අස්විද asvida , n . E. of අශ්විනි .
entries.notes: THE COMPARATIVE RESULT. Every one of the twenty-seven is a Sanskrit/Pali name in Sinhala phonology, and the dictionaries say so themselves rather than leaving it to inference: Carter's formula is literally 'X, n. E. of Y' — Eḷu of — as at අස්විද 'E. of අශ්විනි' (p. 84), දෙනට 'E. of ධනිෂ්ඨ' (p. 297), බෙරණය 'E. of භරණිය' (p. 454), අස්ලිස 'E. of අශේල්ෂාව' (p. 83); Clough's independent formula is 'Elu form of', as at 'Punáwasa ... Elu form of පුනර්වසු' (p. 364) and 'Má-nekat ... Elu form of මඝා maghá' (p. 479). Sinhala replaced NONE of them. Its native coinages — hat-dinna for the Pleiades, ahas-gaṅga for the Milky Way, irabaṭu-taruva and pahan-taruva for Venus, dum-keheliya for a comet, uḷu and taruva for 'star' — all lie OUTSIDE the nakshatra list, in the everyday sky. The one apparent exception is Carter's parse of සිය·වས as '(සිය 100 වස stars)' (p. 682), a native numeral compound for Śatabhiṣaj 'the hundred physicians', and the half-calque මුවසිරස 'deer's head'. Marked 'likely' rather than 'certain' because the numbering is not consistent across sources — Carter counts anura 17th and svāti 15th, Clough counts visākhā 16th, and Carter is internally inconsistent about the 20th/21st (pp. 399, 403, 118). No number has been silently normalised. Sita (Citrā) is the weakest link: it appears in the sources only as Sanskrit චිත්‍තාව, not as an attested Eḷu headword.

caveats: Gundert 1872 is quoted through the DSAL digitisation; his old orthography (ററ for ṟṟ, ളള for ḷḷ) and DSAL's automatic romanization are reproduced as printed, including obvious OCR damage marked /?/. Page numbers are Gundert's own.

Register tagging is the compiler's, applied by a stated rule: 'sanskritic' where the source marks the word S. or Tdbh./tadbhava or Eḷu ('E. of'), i.e. a Sanskrit or Pali word in the local phonology; 'vernacular' where the word is formed from inherited material in the language itself, including calques whose morphemes are all native; 'folk' where the source marks it dialectal, rural, or as an omen/festival term; 'tribal' is used nowhere in this file, since none of these four languages is tribal and no tribal source was reached.

The identification of ഞേങ്ങോല്‍ / മുഴക്കോല്‍ with Orion's Belt is the compiler's inference from Gundert's rising datum, not the source's. Gundert names no stars. It is filed as disputed and should not be cited as an attested identification.

Gundert's own star identifications are occasionally wrong or eccentric and have not been silently corrected: ഋക്ഷം glossed 'Ursa minor' where Sanskrit ṛkṣāḥ is the Great Bear; അത്തം (Hasta) as 'Coma Berenices'; ചിത്ര given as both Spica and 'bright star in Bootes'; ആതിര (Ārdrā) placed in Gemini. Each is flagged in the entry's notes.

For Tulu, the OCR of the Kannada script in Männer 1886/1888 is unusable; every Tulu form here was read from a page image, and one reading — the medial conjunct in ಹೊರಸಿನ್ಟ (Ursa Major) — remains uncertain even at 2400px. Männer's own romanizations are given where he prints them.

Burrow & Emeneau's Dravidian Etymological Dictionary (2nd ed. 1984) is in copyright. It is quoted here only as raw lexical data at minimum length, for attestation of forms that appear nowhere else; the analysis built on it is paraphrase.

Cole 1867 prints Kannada script for Kodava, but the archive.org OCR of it is heavily damaged; the Kodava script forms are reconstructions from the scan checked against Cole's own romanizations, and the romanizations should be preferred where they differ.

Carter's entries tagged 'E. S.' are Carter citing his own English-Sinhalese volume — a signal that the Sinhala is his coinage rather than attested vernacular. Every such item (the Ursa Major bear-calques, sapta-mūnī-cāraya for Charles's Wain, visiṣṭha) is flagged in place and none is counted as vernacular.

Carter p. 61 glosses Arundhatī as 'Pleiades'; this is an error, corrected by Jayatilaka p. 641 to Alcor. Jayatilaka p. 3166 prints Sinhala කුඩාවරහන against the romanization kuḍā-valahā, which do not correspond; that form has therefore been left out of the entries.

Jayatilaka's dictionary is incomplete — the pages reached run only to about ග (p. 4095) — so a 'not in Jayatilaka' result for a headword later in the alphabet means outside coverage, not absent from the language.

The nakshatra numbering differs between and within the sources (Carter counts anura 17th and svāti 15th; Clough counts visākhā 16th; Carter is internally inconsistent about the 20th and 21st; both oscillate between 27 and 28 mansions). No number has been normalised.

Not reached: Indian Antiquary vols. XXIV–XXVI, where Burnell's 'Devil Worship of the Tuluvas' continues (vol. XXIII was searched and contains no star material in the paḍdanas); the Malabar District Gazetteer of Innes & Evans (1908), which could not be located on archive.org and which may carry a fuller ñāṟṟuveḷa table than Gundert's; and any printed source on Lakshadweep or Malabar navigational star-lore, which repeated searching failed to turn up in the public domain.

The Kannada 'karte' system — asterism rain-periods governing sowing, cognate with the Malayalam ñāṟṟuveḷa — is documented for the Lingayats of Bellary in Thurston vol. IV, but Bellary is Kannada country and the passage is therefore comparanda, not an entry in this file.
